title: Dead `if declared is not None:` branch in _format_contract_kwarg — Contract.from_user_declared can never return None once declared_raw is not None
description: Line 96 already guards `if declared_raw is not None:` before calling `declared = Contract.from_user_declared(declared_raw)` (line 97). Contract.from_user_declared returns None ONLY for a None input (haute/_contracts.py:65); every other input either returns a Contract or raises ValueError (it never returns None for a non-None value). Therefore line 98 `if declared is not None:` is always True, and the implicit else (fall through to the get_column_contract path) is unreachable. The defensive guard suggests a fall-through that cannot occur, obscuring the actual control flow (a malformed declared contract raises, it does not silently fall through to contract recomputation).
evidence: _contracts.py Contract.from_user_declared: `if value is None: return None` (65) is the sole None return; '' -> raises (78), {} -> raises (93-96), [] -> raises (105), any unknown type -> raises (105). Given codegen.py:96 already excludes None, `declared` at line 98 is never None. The branch's else (continuing to line 100 try/get_column_contract) can never be taken when declared_raw is truthy.
est_reduction: ~1 line (collapse the redundant guard) + removes a misleading apparent fall-through path
behavior_preservation: Replacing `if declared is not None: return _format_contract_source(...)` with an unconditional `return _format_contract_source(...)` is behaviour-identical because declared is provably non-None here; no input reaches the recompute path via this branch today.
